business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border E-Commerce Overseas Warehouse Order Fulfillment

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (National Jurisdiction), including Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) special regimes
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Codified, with Islamic Sharia as primary source under Article 2 of the Constitution)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-United States Trade and Investment Framework Agreement (TIFA)
Egypt-EU Association Agreement (including investment and trade provisions)
Convention on the Settlement of Investment Disputes between States and Nationals of Other States (ICSID)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014, Law No. 154 of 2019, and its Executive Regulations; Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) regulations on AML/CFT; Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) Rulebook; Commercial Companies Law No. 159 of 1981; Capital Market Law No. 95 of 1992 (for UBO disclosure in listed entities); and the unified registry of beneficial owners established under the 2019 amendments and FRA Decision No. 20 of 2020.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certified Copy of Passport (each non-resident shareholder/UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary public or issuing authority in the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization at the Embassy/Consulate of Egypt (Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Bank Reference Letter (issued within 90 days) for each non-resident shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization at the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney authorizing the Egyptian incorporation agent / local attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization at the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Certificate of Incumbency / Certificate of Good Standing (for corporate shareholders)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization at the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and authorized signatories against (i) United Nations Security Council Consolidated Lists, (ii) Egyptian Terrorist List and terrorist financing list issued by the EGYPT-EMU (Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit), (iii) OFAC SDN List for USD transactions, (iv) EU and UK sanctions lists for secondary exposure, and (v) the CBE's domestic sanctions directive. The screening must be performed prior to client acceptance, updated periodically, and documented in the client due diligence file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Investor Services Portal (gis.gafi.gov.eg) and the Commercial Registry (Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade) electronic name clearance system.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Arabic as the official registered name. An English transliteration is permitted as a secondary display name, provided it is a faithful phonetic transliteration of the Arabic name. The Arabic name must not contain any foreign letters or symbols, and must comply with the standard Arabic alphabetic conventions and the Commercial Registry naming guidelines.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives a written decision from the Commercial Registry or GAFI specifying the ground for refusal under Law No. 159 of 1981 and Executive Regulations. An administrative appeal must be filed with the Commercial Registry's Appeals Committee within 30 days of the rejection date. The appeal must be substantiated with a legal memorandum and a revised name or argument showing non-conflict and compliance with statutory prohibitions. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may challenge the decision before the Administrative Courts of the State Council (Majlis al-Dawla) within 60 days. A reserved name cannot be extended by default; a new application for the same name may be submitted after the 30-day window, but it is subject to a fresh priority check.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for this industry. A physical registered office and actual operational premises (warehouse/facility) are required for obtaining the commercial registry license and the logistics/3PL operational license. GAFI and the Commercial Registry require evidence of a physical address and may reject a purely virtual office arrangement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (estimated 40–60% probability within the first 12 months of operation). The logistics sector and the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) are subject to enhanced physical inspection protocols by the Industrial Development Authority (IDA), the General Authority for the Suez Canal Economic Zone, customs and tax authorities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations; relevant provisions of Civil Code on contracts and commercial registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department, Commercial Registry Office, Cairo.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Tale'el) together with the Founders' Contract (Aqd Ta'sis) and Articles of Association (System Name).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for an Egyptian LLC; however, if the founders declare a capital in the Articles, the amount may be deposited into an Egyptian bank account as a precaution against non-completion, and the bank certificate is filed with GAFI when using the pre-incorporation deposit procedure.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned founders hereby subscribe to the issued shares of EG LLC as stated in the Articles of Association; that the registered office of the Company be established at the address designated in the Articles, within the Arab Republic of Egypt; that [Authorized Manager] be and is hereby appointed as the first manager with authority to execute all incorporation filings with GAFI and the Commercial Registry, open bank accounts, engage the statutory auditor, negotiate warehousing and logistics agreements, and represent the Company before governmental entities; and that the Company adopt a fiscal year ending 31 December and operate in full conformity with Law No. 159/1981 and Investment Law No. 72/2017.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop or GAFI e-Portal (www.ga.gov.eg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an Arabic and English company name search in the relevant commercial register book. Submit preliminary name reservation request with proposed legal form and business activities. After provisional approval, proceed to prepare Arabic MOA and AOA for notarization.
required_dossiers: Copy of founders' national IDs or passports
Proof of legal domicile (lease or title deed) if already identified
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or reserved by a prior entity, file an administrative appeal with GAFI Legal Directorate or submit a modified name within the same candidate list.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Founders' Contract and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary Public in the Governorate of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Contract of Formation and Articles shall be drafted in Arabic stating capital, share percentages, manager's appointment, registered office, and precise business objects covering ISIC 5210 (own-account or third-party fulfillment hub). All founders must sign physically before the notary or execute through duly authorized attorney under authenticated power of attorney.
required_dossiers: Draft Arabic Articles of Association (System Name)
Original/notarized power of attorney if a founder is absent
Bank capital deposit certificate if capital is declared and paid
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notary identifies inconsistencies, correct signatures, correct the Arabic transliteration of non-Egyptian names, or amend capital provisions by supplementary notarial instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Filing and Commercial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department and Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File notarized MOA/AOA and obtain establishment order from GAFI. Pay registration fees and stamp duties. Enter company into the Commercial Register and obtain the Commercial Registration Certificate indicating the company's legal form.
required_dossiers: Lease contract for registered office (with certified copy)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the stated object or registered office, submit a written clarification letter, attach a revised Articles of Association, and request a formal review before the GAFI complaints committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Central Department for Registration and Taxpayer Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File tax card application online or at the ETA office, incorporating the Commercial Registration Certificate. Register for corporate income tax, VAT, and payroll withholding. Obtain the Tax Card and a VAT certificate if annual taxable supplies exceed the VAT registration threshold.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Articles of Association
Power of attorney if represented by a tax agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If late or incomplete registration is indicated, pay the nominal delay fine and submit a waiver/facility application under ETA reconciliation procedures; provide all missing supporting certificates quickly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Insurance Registration and Municipal Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) and local Governorate Municipality Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LLC as an employer with NOSI for employees' social insurance. Obtain necessary municipal licensing for the registered office and, if conducting on-site cargo handling, a business establishment permit with the civil defense approval for warehouse occupancy.
required_dossiers: Lease contract certified by the real estate owner
Civil Defense fire safety clearance (preliminary for warehouse)
List of founding employees and salary declarations for NOSI
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of municipal zoning refusal or incomplete civil defense clearance, apply for license modification, supply structural engineer's certificate, and request re-inspection of the warehouse void usage.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Authority for Industrial Development (IDA) for ancillary light processing; Ministry of Trade and Industry and the competent Local Municipal Licensing Unit for warehouse/commercial logistics approval.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Warehousing and Logistics Operating License – Inclusive of Cross-Border E-Commerce Order Fulfillment Activity (Industrial/Commercial Establishment License).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (Registration / Small-Scale Non-Hazardous Facility) for a cross-docking and fulfillment warehouse that does not process or manufacture hazardous materials; full EIA is not required unless the facility exceeds storage thresholds or uses significant generators.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance required with Law No. 4/1994 as amended by Law No. 9/2009: wastewater discharge to public sewers must meet the limits set by Law No. 93/1962, and the EIA guidelines for ambient air, including limits on suspended solids, VOC fugitive emissions from any cleaning agents, and proper labeling for non-hazardous waste. Waste storage must be covered and segregated; no open burning is permitted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification from the Civil Defense Authority must certify adequate emergency exits, fire extinguishing systems, smoke detection, and clear access lanes; structural load inspection by a licensed engineer confirming the floor capacity for racking and forklift traffic; and the Ministry of Manpower shall inspect that the warehouse employer provides adequate ventilation, first aid equipment, and a compliant occupational safety and health program.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) under the Ministry of Finance; official ETA digital portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg, with integrated e-invoicing, e-receipt, taxpayer registration and tax card services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Egyptian LLC or a foreign LLC branch engaged in cross-dock/3PL fulfillment: (1) complete corporate existence/investment registration with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) and the Commercial Registry; (2) legalize the foreign incorporation/charter, power of attorney and board resolutions in Arabic and obtain the required apostille/consular legalization; (3) file the LLC or branch registration documents with GAFI and obtain the investment/commercial registration number; (4) submit the ETA taxpayer registration application at the competent tax office with the GAFI certificate, constitution/charter, local lease or service address evidence, local statutory representative passport, and board resolution, after which the ETA issues the unified Tax Card carrying the Tax Identification Number (TIN); (5) apply separately for VAT registration under VAT Law 67/2016 as soon as the mandatory registration threshold is met or before making the first taxable supply, and activate the ETA e-invoicing/e-receipt account with a certified digital signature. A foreign entity without a branch cannot ordinarily obtain a standalone TIN/VAT ID; the in-country LLC/branch is the statutory Egyptian taxpayer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt has no check-the-box or pass-through election for LLCs: an Egyptian LLC is a per se corporation for income tax purposes and a separate VAT person. No hybrid mismatch or entity-classification election is available. Limited administrative elections exist: voluntary VAT registration from the EGP 250,000 turnover level, VAT grouping or consolidated VAT registration where the ETA recognizes common control, investment incentive regimes in Special Economic Zones/free zones, and depreciation method elections under Law 91/2005.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended, administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority; replaces the old General Sales Tax and applies to taxable supplies of goods and services in Egypt and to imports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration where annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000; voluntary registration is available where annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 250,000. The ETA may also require registration before the threshold where a taxpayer makes an importation or first taxable supply, and foreign digital/e-commerce suppliers making taxable Egyptian supplies may have separate registration obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory ETA e-invoicing and e-receipt clearance applies to VAT-registered taxpayers. Invoices must be transmitted from certified ERP/billing software through the ETA API in prescribed XML/JSON schema, digitally signed with the taxpayer’s ETA certificate, and validated by the ETA before becoming fiscally valid. Accepted invoices receive a unique ETA acceptance code/QR digital stamp; B2B/B2G invoices are cleared in near-real-time, while B2C e-receipt clearance is phased in. Non-compliant invoices are rejected and can deny input VAT deduction. For cross-dock/3PL activity, inventory transfers to the warehouse are not taxable supplies but must be documented consistent with the principal/seller invoicing arrangement to preserve export zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods exported outside Egypt and to internationally connected services (international transport, handling, packing, commission and port services) supplied to or paid by non-residents, provided the exporter is VAT-registered; the goods physically leave Egypt within the statutory export window (generally 90 days from invoice, extendable on ETA/Customs approval); a customs export declaration is filed in the exporter’s name; the sale is made to a non-resident under a foreign-currency contract; the goods are not diverted to domestic consumption; and input VAT invoices are properly matched to the export supply. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports is creditable and refundable through ETA after documentary matching.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration and officially stamped terminal/port release records evidencing physical departure from Egypt
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR or equivalent transport document naming a consignee outside Egypt
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice from an Egyptian bank evidencing receipt of the export proceeds in convertible foreign exchange
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA can re-audit export transactions retrospectively and reverse zero-rating where documentation is missing, mismatched or backdated, requiring output VAT plus reversal of input VAT credits/refunds. Late payment surcharges accrue on assessed tax, and administrative fines under VAT Law 67/2016 apply for invoice, declaration and documentation violations. Fraudulent export claims, including forged customs declarations, bills of lading or inward remittance certificates, circular foreign-currency receipts, or fabricated cross-dock movements, can result in disgorgement of refunded VAT, additional fines calculated by reference to evaded tax, suspension or blacklisting of the taxpayer’s TIN/e-invoicing account, and criminal prosecution of the entity and responsible officers. A cross-dock/3PL operator must avoid holding export documents merely for a related principal while recording local fulfillment services, which may be re-characterized as taxable Egyptian service revenue and trigger clawback of the principal’s export zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — sole monetary and exchange-control regulator under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law), as amended; CBE licenses all authorized banks and non-bank FX bureaus, operates and supervises the interbank foreign-exchange market, issues binding FX circulars, enforces AML/CFT obligations under AML Law No. 80 of 2002, and administers Egypt's unified flexible-exchange-rate framework adopted in March 2024 and fully liberalized in December 2024; the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) handles investment registration but exercises no independent FX regulatory authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The EGP is freely convertible for all current-account transactions — import/export settlement, 3PL and logistics service fees, dividend and profit remittance, and intra-group service payments — through CBE-authorized banks at the prevailing interbank rate; capital-account transactions, including foreign-currency borrowing by Egyptian residents, issuance of guarantees abroad, and outbound portfolio investment, remain restricted and require CBE approval or mandatory registration with an authorized bank; non-resident shareholders of an EG LLC may remit dividends and liquidation proceeds after satisfying Egyptian withholding tax (10% standard, treaty-reduced where applicable), submission of audited financial statements, ETA tax clearance, and production of the GAFI investment-file registration; practical remittance hurdles are documentary rather than administrative, including transfer-pricing review of intercompany fees and transient USD liquidity conditions, though the 2025 normalization of foreign-currency availability has materially reduced delay.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters of goods and services, including cross-border e-commerce fulfillment and cross-dock 3PL operators, must repatriate 100% of proceeds to Egypt through a CBE-authorized bank within 180 days from the date of customs release (goods) or from the contractual invoice/settlement date (services); the exporter must file the export declaration, commercial invoice, customs manifest, and marketplace settlement statements to enable the bank's underlying-trade review; the mandatory conversion-to-EGP surrender percentage was rescinded in March 2024, allowing proceeds to be retained in foreign-currency accounts and converted at the interbank rate only when EGP operational liquidity is required; the CBE retains emergency authority to reinstate surrender ratios, and non-compliance triggers penalty interest at the statutory banking rate, suspension of FX services, and delisting from CBE watch reports.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / USD Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium as a primary banking channel and Not Permitted as a substitute for an Egyptian licensed bank: foreign digital EMIs (Airwallex, Wise Business, Payoneer, Currencycloud) hold no Egyptian banking license, cannot maintain EGP nostro accounts, and cannot perform CBE-authorized FX; they are viable only as offshore collection and payout layers for marketplace receipts (Amazon, Noon, Shopify, AliExpress) in USD/EUR/GBP, with onward SWIFT MT103 routing to the EG LLC's onshore Egyptian bank account; all domestic EGP payments — payroll, VAT/ETA settlement, supplier disbursements — must settle through a licensed Egyptian bank under AML Law No. 80 of 2002 and CBE payment-oversight rules; Airwallex Global Accounts may receive cross-border e-commerce payouts, but onboarding must be combined with a physical Egyptian bank account and the EMI's anti-money-laundering and sanctions-screening standards must meet CBE/FATF expectations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical presence for corporate account opening: CBE consolidated AML/KYC rules and AML Law No. 80 of 2002 require face-to-face verification of the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and all authorized signatories before account activation; remote or fully digital corporate onboarding is not permitted — CBE restricts electronic e-KYC to natural persons for basic accounts; non-resident directors must either appear personally at the bank's Egyptian branch, execute signature specimen before an attorney holding a notarized power of attorney legalized by the Egyptian consulate, or complete consular KYC at an Egyptian embassy/consulate where the bank approves such protocol; the bank's compliance officer also conducts a formal interview (physical or video based on bank policy) and, for fulfillment entities, a site inspection of the registered office and warehouse address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and shareholder opacity: non-resident shareholders structured through offshore holding companies or nominee layers trigger enhanced due diligence and automatic escalation to the bank's AML committee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and constitutional documents of the ultimate parent, full UBO register with passport copies and proof-of-address issues within 3 months, GAFI investment-file registration and Form 1 investment declaration, corporate-structure diagram, signed source-of-wealth statement with supporting bank statements for each material shareholder, and, for nominee arrangements, the executed declaration of trust and settlor identification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce marketplace settlement opacity: recurring cross-border payouts from multiple platforms or pooled PSP/EMI accounts raise suspicion of revenue laundering, unlicensed money transmission, or factoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed platform service agreements, 12 months of marketplace payout reports and settlement statements, PSP transaction history, order-level warehouse manifests and customs EDI files, client 3PL agreements with issued invoices, and an independent accountant's report reconciling revenue to marketplace reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and financial-crime screening hits: matches against OFAC, UN, or EU sanctions lists, counterparties in high-risk jurisdictions, or shipments to sanctioned proxy buyers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions-screening policy using accredited tools (World-Check, Refinitiv), scrubbed customer and counterparty lists, Egyptian Ministry of Trade export licenses for restricted goods, end-user certificates, and a legal opinion on OFAC/UN/UK sanctions compliance confirming no designated-party nexus in the supply chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Purpose-code and customs mismatch: wire references inconsistent with the declared 3PL/cross-dock business, or discrepancies between customs declarations, warehouse records, and commercial invoices during the bank's underlying-trade review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Reconciled transaction ledger matching customs declarations to invoices and warehouse receipts, inbound/outbound warehouse manifests, bills of lading and airway bills, packing lists, and fully completed bank 'declaration of transaction purpose' forms with the correct service-export narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax and commercial-registry gaps: expired commercial registration, ETA tax card or VAT certificate, or unresolved ETA assessments causing the bank to block dividend or FX remittances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current commercial-registry extract, ETA tax card including VAT registration under GST Law No. 67 of 2016, evidence of payroll and withholding-tax filings, social-insurance compliance certificate, and an ETA no-objection or tax-clearance letter.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections and shareholder loans must be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the overseas remitting bank to the EG LLC's foreign-currency account at an authorized Egyptian bank, with field 70 references stating 'Capital Increase—FDI', 'Shareholder Loan—GAFI File [number]', or 'Operating Funding—LLC [CR number]', and the remitter name matching the shareholder register; for formal equity increases, the LLC must file the capital-increase resolution with GAFI, update the investment ledger, and amend the commercial registry before the bank credits the capital-escalation sub-account; intercompany shareholder loans must be evidenced by a signed loan agreement and registered in the CBE's electronic foreign-borrowing database at the authorized bank to secure future remittance of principal and interest; the bank issues an inward-remittance certificate, and any mismatched remitter name, missing purpose code, or unregistered loan will cause automatic rejection or post-hoc blocking of future FX repatriation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for overseas suppliers, international freight, 3PL sub-contractors, and royalties may be executed through: (a) SWIFT MT103/MT202 direct documentary remittance against commercial invoice — the standard rail for e-commerce logistics costs; (b) sight or usance Commercial Letters of Credit opened through the Egyptian bank with customs import documentation, applicable since the 2023 repeal of the mandatory-LC regime; (c) documentary collections (DP/DA) and open-account transfers for low-risk, repeat counterparties; and (d) domestic EGP settlement via CBE's EG-ACH (InstantPay) and RTGS for local warehouse rents, payroll, and vendor payments; for outbound transfers above USD 250,000, the bank requires ETA tax clearance, transfer-pricing documentation for related-party fees, and compliance with the declared interbank rate with settlement in no more than T+2.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX Forwards on EGP/USD with documented underlying trade or service exposure, tenor typically up to 180 days, executed at authorized banks on interbank forward points
FX Swaps (spot-forward combinations) between authorized banks and corporate clients for liquidity and currency-translation management with registered underlying flows
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) for USD/EGP intercompany loan exposure, subject to CBE authorization and bank credit-line approval
Vanilla FX Options (plain puts and calls) on EGP/USD permitted at authorized banks with CBE notification, used to hedge budgeted receivable or payable exposures

Offshore Currency Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on EGP permitted only through offshore desks or foreign counterparties outside Egypt; not settled onshore and requiring documentary proof of underlying trade exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return for the LLC and audited financial statements in support of the return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Corporate Tax Department, electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April following the 31 December fiscal year-end; for an approved non-calendar year, within four months after the close of the tax period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a monthly late-payment surcharge of 2% of the unpaid tax for each month or part-month; the ETA may issue a best-evidence assessment, suspend tax clearance, and enforce collection by seizure of bank accounts. Chronic non-filing after formal notifications is a ground for administrative strike-off from the Commercial Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited annual financial statements, auditor’s report, and shareholders’ approval record deposited with the companies registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Directorate, with complementary filing at the Commercial Registry Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the balance-sheet date, i.e., by 30 June for a calendar-year LLC; the shareholders' approval is recorded at the ordinary general assembly before filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may prevent issuance of tax clearance and commercial-registry extracts; after repeated administrative notice, the registry may initiate dissolution proceedings of the LLC. Directors/managers may be held personally liable for outstanding filing obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ultimate-beneficial-owner (UBO) confirmation and share-transfer update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Corporate Registry / UBO Register integrated with the Commercial Registry single window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March following the end of the calendar year; any transfer of membership interest must be updated in the statutory members’ register and filed with GAFI within 30 days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliant UBO data is subject to an administrative penalty of up to EGP 100,000 (approximately USD 2,150) under the Egyptian AML/Companies Law regime; a suspended UBO file blocks all commercial-registry transactions and may lead to strike-off in cases of repeated, uncorrected default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Egyptian Companies Law, an LLC is required to appoint at least one certified public accountant as auditor at each ordinary shareholders’ meeting. A statutory independent audit is mandatory for every LLC regardless of revenue or total assets, and the auditor must be licensed and registered in Egypt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), issued under Egyptian Ministerial Decree No. 110/2015 (as amended), substantially aligned with IFRS; for income-tax purposes the accounting profit is reconciled to the taxable profit under Law No. 91 of 2005.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a UBO register identifying every individual who ultimately owns or controls 10% or more of the LLC or otherwise exercises control through ownership, rights, or voting arrangements. The annual confirmation is filed with GAFI by 31 March each year; any share transfer during the year is recorded in the members’ register and submitted to GAFI within 30 days, with the year-end confirmation restating the current UBO list or certifying that no change occurred. Failure to update after a transfer prevents the transferee from voting and exposes the managers to liability.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders’ and Managers’ resolutions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Investment Law 72/2017 may grant a 50% CIT reduction for up to 5 tax years for qualifying logistics and warehousing projects satisfying labor, technology, or capital criteria; entities licensed inside GAFI Free Zones or the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) can qualify for full CIT exemption on eligible goods-based profits, subject to annual licence fees and activity compliance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 19 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-services portal, www.eta.gov.eg, including the ETA integrated e-filing and e-payment system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months after the close of the fiscal year, per Article 85 of Law 91 of 2005; for a calendar-year taxpayer, no later than 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Identification and Tax Card Data
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, commercial registration number, tax card number, 10-digit TIN, address of the Egyptian warehouse, fiscal year start and end dates, and activity code under the ETA business register.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident principal operating through the Egyptian 3PL warehouse as a permanent establishment must complete this box using the Egyptian PE registration details, not the offshore head office details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total invoiced revenue for cross-dock handling, storage, order fulfilment, repacking, last-mile coordination, and any separately billed ancillary services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Egypt-source revenue attributable to the Egyptian PE. Revenue booked remotely by the foreign head office for services performed entirely outside Egypt should be excluded and separately supported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, wages, warehousing rent, depreciation on material handling equipment, utilities, shipping and freight costs, IT platform expenses, customs brokers, and other P&L items satisfying the deduction rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Head-office recharge allocations are deductible only where the corresponding services are actually rendered, beneficial to the Egyptian PE, and supported by transfer pricing documentation at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Taxable Income Before Loss Set-Off
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit adjusted for disallowed expenses, provisions, timing differences, and any transfer pricing adjustments mandated by the ETA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident principal with an Egyptian PE, taxable income is limited to profits economically attributable to the PE; no overseas group overheads may be deducted without a compliant TP analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declared prior-year tax losses utilized against current-year taxable income, subject to the 5-year carryforward limitation and continuity-of-activity rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border loss pooling is not permitted; losses generated by the Egyptian PE are only available to offset future Egyptian PE income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Advance Payments and Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly corporate tax instalments already paid, plus any final withholding tax credits, deducted from the total computed tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only credits statutorily available to the Egyptian PE may be claimed; foreign home-country notional taxes or head-office losses cannot be credited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by the 22.5% statutory corporate income tax rate, reduced by eligible credits and offset by installed payments, yielding the final balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The flat 22.5% rate applies to the PE's Egyptian attributable income; dividend withholding tax on downstream remittances is not settled through this box.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a monthly surcharge of 2% of the total tax due for each commenced month of delay, an administrative fine up to EGP 50,000, denial of tax clearance certificates, and risk of enforced collection, bank attachment, or warehouse asset seizure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Transfer Pricing Disclosure Return (ETA TP annex) submitted together with Form 19 through the ETA e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same statutory deadline as Form 19; the TP disclosure must be filed within 4 months after the fiscal year-end or no later than the extended filing date granted by the ETA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of all related-party transactions, including intercompany warehouse services, logistics fees, management charges, software licences, interest, and recharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident groups must disclose any cross-border arrangement in which the Egyptian PE pays or receives value from group entities, including cost-sharing or global service fee schemes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selection of the transfer pricing method, comparable data source, financial ratios, and arm's-length range calibration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the benchmarking or comparability study for the Egyptian fulfilment functions and risk profile; state the tested party and rationale clearly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signed declaration by the legal representative and certified tax accountant confirming the accuracy of the TP disclosures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian PE general manager or authorised power-of-attorney holder must sign; remote electronic signature by the foreign CFO is not sufficient without an Egyptian tax representative.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failing to file the TP disclosure or Local File triggers fines in the range of EGP 10,000 to EGP 100,000, upward TP adjustments plus annual interest at 18.5%, and may escalate to criminal tax evasion treatment for wilful concealment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly Advance CIT Payment Schedule submitted through the ETA e-payment microservice within the official filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Self-assessed advance corporate tax instalments are payable on the ETA-prescribed quarterly dates relative to the fiscal year, generally within 30 days after each quarter-end, with the final settlement made on the annual Form 19.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated taxable profit for the fiscal year, applied to the 22.5% rate, divided into advance instalments, with declared actual quarter profit for any variance required by the ETA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PEs must instal based on realistically projected Egypt-source profits; using zero instalments while generating Egyptian fulfilment revenue will attract delay surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique payment reference number, TIN, and fiscal year designation of each quarter paid; linkage of payments to the annual return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign treasury teams must remit each instalment through an Egyptian-licensed bank using the PE tax account reference; cross-border payments without CBE authorisation are unlawful.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Each unpaid or late quarterly instalment attracts a monthly 2% surcharge of the amount due and can trigger administrative freezing of bank accounts until settlement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke an applicable double tax agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must (i) obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority for the distribution year, (ii) provide a beneficial-ownership declaration and subsidiary substance evidence, and (iii) submit the application to the ETA International Taxation Department before or at the date of distribution. If the ETA recognises the DTA, the reduced rate is applied at source; where no prior approval has been obtained, the statutory 10% rate is withheld and a refund claim may be filed through the ETA within the applicable limitation period, supported by the TRC and complete ownership documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates under Law 91 of 2005 are 20% for royalty payments to non-residents and 20% for interest paid to non-resident lenders. Under Egypt's tax treaty network, rates are typically reduced to 10% to 20% for interest and 15% to 20% for royalties, subject to beneficial-ownership analysis, TRC submission, and application of the Principal Purpose Test.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 8,000,000 in aggregate controlled transactions within a tax period triggers mandatory Local File documentation; Master File and CbC notification requirements arise for multinational groups with consolidated revenue equal to or exceeding EGP 15,000,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has no UAE-style standalone Economic Substance Regulations; however, Article 31 of Law 91 of 2005 contains a general anti-abuse rule empowering the ETA to disregard transactions lacking bona fide commercial substance. For treaty relief and CIT purposes, the EG LLC must demonstrate actual staff, warehouse capacity, inventory control systems, decision-making records, and risk assumption in Egypt; a shell or letterbox structure claiming DTA benefits will be attacked under the substance-over-form doctrine and treaty anti-abuse provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing false Form 19 returns, suppressing Egypt-source cross-dock revenue, fabricating logistics expenses, using forged e-invoices or QR-coded fake invoices, or maintaining dual books for the Egyptian fulfilment operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of up to 5 years, a fine of up to EGP 50,000, double collection of the evaded tax, monthly delay surcharges of 2%, administrative attachment of bank accounts and warehouse assets, and suspension of commercial registration and tax clearance certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, tax managers, and signatories of false returns may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax and penalties; travel bans, passport stays, asset freezes, and arrest warrants may be issued personally, and the corporate veil can be pierced where fraud is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the annual TP disclosure, omitting intercompany warehouse or head-office service transactions, charging non-arm's-length margins for cross-dock services, or refusing to provide the Local File upon ETA request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA transfer pricing adjustment to the arm's-length result, annual interest on the underpayment at 18.5%, fines between EGP 10,000 and EGP 100,000, disallowance of intercompany deductions, and referral for criminal evasion charges for deliberate concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally engineered artificial intercompany pricing face personal civil claims for restitution; in severe cases, criminal liability attaches and travel bans or property attachment are invoked to enforce tax debt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal Profit Repatriation and Foreign Exchange Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Disguising dividend distributions as inflated management fees or fake royalty charges, effecting foreign currency remittances through unlicensed informal money brokers (hawala), or repatriating profits without ETA withholding tax settlement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of the 10% dividend WHT plus 2% monthly delay penalties; fines under the Central Bank of Egypt and foreign exchange framework ranging from EGP 1,000,000 to EGP 10,000,000, imprisonment from 6 months to 5 years for unlicensed FX dealing, and freezing of corporate and beneficiary bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with operational knowledge of unlawful FX remittance schemes face criminal prosecution, personal fines, asset seizure, travel bans, and possible extradition; board approval receipts will not shield individual culpability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Shell Company Misuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the EG LLC as a shell conduit for third-party funds, hiding ultimate beneficial owners of the fulfilment enterprise, structuring cash deposits to evade Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering reporting thresholds, or laundering proceeds derived from sanctioned markets through warehousing transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egyptian AML Law 80 of 2002, imprisonment from 3 to 7 years, fines up to EGP 500,000 or twice the laundered amount, confiscation of warehouse inventory and bank balances, forfeiture of corporate assets, and blacklisting from export and re-export facilitation programs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly facilitate predicate laundering acts are personally criminally liable; personal assets are subject to seizure, passports are lifted, and Interpol red notices may be issued for fugitive principals.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to issue e-invoices or e-receipts for cross-dock services, not registering material handling equipment in the ETA asset ledger, failing to file the annual return and TP disclosure, or missing quarterly advance instalments deliberately.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monthly 2% surcharge on the unpaid tax for each commenced month of default, administrative fines up to EGP 50,000, nullity of deduction claims for undocumented expenses, suspension of the legal representative's tax signature, and inclusion in the public ETA defaulters list.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and certified accountant who signed non-compliant digital filings are exposed to administrative fines in their personal capacity; directors who ignore ETA recovery orders may face property attachment and travel restrictions until the corporate debt is serviced.
